_README: questions_draft.json — WORKING FILE for the gold-dataset authoring loop.
This file is NOT committed to the experimental run. It is the scratchpad
you use while authoring candidate questions. The committed files are:
1. Pick a category. Replace the example question below with a real one.
Start with simple_address — easiest. Set expected_facts to []
for now; you'll fill it in after step 2.
2. Run the runner against this draft (from inside llm-service/):
← see what the SQL/vector layer actually returned. This is your
ground truth for what is in the DB.
← eval_scores.issues hints at expected_constraints to add.
/ must_avoid based on the cache file (NOT the LLM answer).
4. Loop until you have N questions for that category. Move them
5. After all 20 are authored, hand-pick 5 for questions_smoke.json:
1 edge_case (Option 2 split — no numeric_aggregation or comparative).
category               str    one of: simple_address, constraint_filtering,
in VALID_CATEGORIES but EXPECTED count is 0
difficulty             str    one of: easy, medium, hard
question               str    the user-facing question text
hint_address           str?   if exactly one address is in the question,
mirror it here so the runner sets
expected_facts         list   atomic, checkable claims a correct answer
must contain. one per element. fill in
expected_numeric       dict?  keys are short names (e.g. matching_count,
atemp_m2), values numeric. omit if not numeric.
expected_constraints   list   filtering / scoping clauses the answer
must_avoid             list   patterns the answer must NOT contain.
notes                  str    one-sentence rationale: which axis this
stresses, which router branch fires, gotchas.
created_at             str    ISO 8601 UTC, set once at authoring time.
TARGET COUNTS (must match exactly for validate_dataset.py to pass):
Option 2 split — set 2026-05-10 after Step 0.5.2 walkthrough.
numeric_aggregation    0  ← dropped (DeSO routes to broken Specialized SQL)
